title: ProvenanceEnvelope
description: The envelope every claim-bearing record in OVIP must carry. A claim without provenance is not expressible in this protocol. Fields marked serverDerived are computed by the implementation; an instance submitted by a client containing one MUST be rejected with 400 naming the offending field, never silently sanitised.

source.description: The channel that produced this claim. Server-derived.

evidence_refs.description: Evidence backing this claim. An empty array is legal and forces trust_level T0.

observation_id.description: The Observation this claim was extracted from, where one exists.

confidence.description: Extraction fidelity, NOT trust. How reliably the value was read or parsed. An OCR engine can be 0.99 confident about a value read perfectly off a forged document. Server-derived.

trust_level.description: Computed corroboration level. Never author-supplied; recomputable from the record and its evidence. See docs/TRUST_MODEL.md.

anchoring.description: Tamper-evidence state, ORTHOGONAL to trust_level. T4 in prose. An anchored T0 claim is a self-declaration that provably has not been edited — it is still a self-declaration. Implementations MUST display this separately from trust_level and MUST NOT render it as verification.

observed_at.description: When the underlying fact was observed, if different from asserted_at.

issuer.description: DID of the Issuer, when the claim is issuer-signed. Server-derived from the verified signature, never from the payload.

access_scope.description: public | professional | restricted. The live implementation persists 'restricted' as the string 'mythos_private'; see docs/PRIVACY_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.
